title: Michigan's 6th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Michigan's 6th Congressional District will feature incumbent Democrat Debbie Dingell seeking re-election against Republican challenger Heather Smiley. The district encompasses all of Washtenaw County, parts of Wayne County, and portions of Monroe and Oakland Counties, including communities such as Ann Arbor, Dearborn, and Woodhaven. Michigan utilizes an open primary system, with the primary scheduled for August 4, 2026. Dingell has held the seat since 2023 following redistricting and previously represented Michigan's 12th District from 2015 to 2023.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 race in Michigan's 6th Congressional District as of the research date.

candidates.name: Debbie Dingell
candidates.summary: Debbie Dingell is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2014 to succeed her late husband, the longest-serving member of Congress in U.S. history. She serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and the House Natural Resources Committee, chairs the House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee, and co-chairs the Great Lakes Task Force. Prior to Congress, she worked for over three decades in the auto industry, serving as President of the General Motors Foundation and as a senior executive in public affairs, and chaired the Wayne State University Board of Governors.

candidates.name: Heather Smiley
candidates.summary: Heather Smiley is a Republican candidate running for U.S. House in Michigan's 6th Congressional District. She is a retired Ford Motor Company employee with over 32 years of service in product development, strategy and planning, business reengineering, and analytics. Smiley is a first-generation college graduate who earned both bachelor's and master's degrees from Central Michigan University, and has served as a community volunteer first responder and instructor. She previously challenged incumbent Debbie Dingell in the 2024 general election.

forecast.rationale: No public polls exist for this race, so confidence is medium despite strong structural signals. However, the available district and candidate data point to a safe Democratic hold. Michigan's 6th District encompasses all of Washtenaw County (including Ann Arbor) and parts of Wayne County (including Dearborn), two of the most Democratic areas in the state. Incumbent Debbie Dingell is a well-established, institutionally powerful figure — chair of the House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee, co-chair of the Great Lakes Task Force — who has held this seat or adjacent territory since 2015, preceded by her late husband John Dingell (the longest-serving member of Congress). Republican challenger Heather Smiley is a repeat opponent from 2024 with a strong professional background but no public polling, fundraising data, or other evidence of a race that has become competitive. The district was drawn in the 2022 redistricting cycle as a safely Democratic seat. Without polls, the forecast relies on these structural fundamentals, which overwhelmingly favor the incumbent.
